config.title: Build keyboard shortcut manager

intro.title: Build keyboard shortcut manager
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a keyboard shortcut manager that allows users to trigger specific actions by pressing key combinations. You will learn how to handle keyboard events in JavaScript to detect when keys are pressed. The core programming concepts involved include event listeners, conditional logic, and managing state for active shortcuts. This project will help you understand how to create interactive web applications that respond to user input efficiently.
intro.usecase: Keyboard shortcuts are essential productivity features in professional software where users perform repetitive tasks. Developers implement them in code editors like VS Code for commands (Ctrl+S to save), in design tools like Figma for quick actions (V for selection tool), and in data dashboards for filtering and navigation. Mastering keyboard shortcut management allows you to build more efficient interfaces where power users can work faster without reaching for the mouse.

objectives: Implement a function to capture and process keyboard events
Construct a data structure to store keyboard shortcut mappings
Bind keyboard event listeners to the document or specific elements
Manipulate the DOM to display active shortcut status
Initialize and update shortcut configurations dynamically
Integrate multiple shortcut combinations for different actions
Control event propagation and prevent default browser behavior

steps.title: Import required modules
steps.instruction: Import the necessary modules for the keyboard shortcut manager. You'll need to import React and the useState hook from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the React library and useState hook available for building the keyboard shortcut manager.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for building the keyboard shortcut manager.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create main keyboard shortcut manager function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'keyboardShortcutManager' that returns an empty object for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Make sure it returns an empty object {}.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and useState here

// Create the keyboardShortcutManager function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'keyboardShortcutManager' is defined and returns an empty object.
successCriteria: The function 'keyboardShortcutManager' is defined and returns an empty object {}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main function that will manage keyboard shortcuts.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it's named 'keyboardShortcutManager' and returns an empty object {}.
steps.feedbackWrong: Please create a function named 'keyboardShortcutManager' that returns an empty object.

steps.title: Initialize shortcuts storage object
steps.instruction: Inside the keyboardShortcutManager function, create an empty object named shortcuts to store registered keyboard shortcuts.
steps.hint: You can declare a variable with const and assign an empty object {} to it.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating an empty object for storage
const items = {};
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will have a shortcuts object ready to store keyboard shortcuts.
successCriteria: A variable named shortcuts is declared and initialized as an empty object inside the keyboardShortcutManager function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the shortcuts object to store keyboard shortcuts.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've declared a variable named shortcuts and assigned an empty object {} to it inside the function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The shortcuts object wasn't created correctly. Check that you declared it inside the keyboardShortcutManager function.

steps.title: Create function to register shortcuts
steps.instruction: Inside the keyboardShortcutManager function, define a function named registerShortcut that takes two parameters: key and action.
steps.hint: Add a function declaration inside keyboardShortcutManager. The function should be able to receive a key string and an action callback.
steps.expectedOutcome: The keyboardShortcutManager function now contains a nested registerShortcut function that can receive key and action parameters.
successCriteria: A function named registerShortcut is defined inside keyboardShortcutManager with parameters key and action.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the registerShortcut function. This will allow users to add new keyboard shortcuts to the manager.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure registerShortcut is defined inside keyboardShortcutManager and accepts both key and action parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The registerShortcut function needs to be defined inside keyboardShortcutManager with two parameters: key and action.

steps.title: Create function to remove shortcuts
steps.instruction: Inside the keyboardShortcutManager function, define a function named removeShortcut that takes a key parameter and deletes that key from the shortcuts object.
steps.hint: You can use the delete operator to remove a property from an object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The keyboardShortcutManager function will now have a removeShortcut function that can delete shortcuts from the manager.
successCriteria: A function named removeShortcut is defined inside keyboardShortcutManager, takes a key parameter, and uses delete to remove that key from the shortcuts object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the removeShortcut function. This allows the manager to clean up shortcuts when they're no longer needed.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your removeShortcut function properly deletes the key from the shortcuts object using the delete operator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The removeShortcut function isn't quite right. Remember to define it inside keyboardShortcutManager, take a key parameter, and use delete shortcuts[key] to remove the shortcut.

steps.title: Create function to check key combinations
steps.instruction: Inside the keyboardShortcutManager function, create a helper function named checkKeyCombination that takes a key parameter and returns true if that key exists in the shortcuts object, otherwise false.
steps.hint: Define a function that checks if the given key exists as a property in the shortcuts object. You can use the 'in' operator or hasOwnProperty method.
steps.expectedOutcome: A checkKeyCombination function that validates whether a key combination is registered.
successCriteria: The checkKeyCombination function is defined inside keyboardShortcutManager and correctly checks key existence in shortcuts.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the validation function that will help determine if a keyboard combination is registered.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it properly checks if the key exists in the shortcuts object and returns a boolean value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The checkKeyCombination function should validate key combinations by checking if they exist in the shortcuts object.

steps.title: Create event handler for keydown events
steps.instruction: Inside the keyboardShortcutManager function, define a function named handleKeyDown that takes an event parameter.
steps.hint: Create a function that will process keyboard events when keys are pressed.
steps.expectedOutcome: The keyboardShortcutManager function will contain a handleKeyDown function that can receive keyboard events.
successCriteria: A handleKeyDown function is defined inside keyboardShortcutManager with an event parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the event handler function that will process keyboard events.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've defined a function named handleKeyDown with an event parameter inside keyboardShortcutManager.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleKeyDown function isn't properly defined. Create a function named handleKeyDown that takes an event parameter inside keyboardShortcutManager.

steps.title: Add event listener for keyboard events
steps.instruction: Inside the keyboardShortcutManager function, add an event listener to the document that listens for 'keydown' events and calls the handleKeyDown function (which you'll create in the next step).
steps.hint: Use document.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown) to attach the event listener. Place this inside the keyboardShortcutManager function before the return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: The keyboardShortcutManager function now includes an event listener that will trigger the handleKeyDown function when any key is pressed.
successCriteria: The document.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown) line is added inside the keyboardShortcutManager function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the event listener that will capture keyboard events.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're adding document.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown) inside the keyboardShortcutManager function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to add an event listener to the document that listens for 'keydown' events and calls handleKeyDown.

steps.title: Create function to get all registered shortcuts
steps.instruction: Inside the keyboardShortcutManager function, define a new function named getAllShortcuts that returns the current shortcuts object.
steps.hint: Create a function that simply returns the shortcuts object. This will allow external code to see what shortcuts are currently registered.
steps.expectedOutcome: The getAllShortcuts function should be defined inside keyboardShortcutManager and return the shortcuts object.
successCriteria: The getAllShortcuts function is defined and returns the shortcuts object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the getAllShortcuts function. This provides a way to view all registered keyboard shortcuts.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the function, but make sure it's named getAllShortcuts and returns the shortcuts object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The getAllShortcuts function is not properly defined. It should be inside keyboardShortcutManager and return the shortcuts object.

steps.title: Export the keyboard shortcut manager
steps.instruction: Export the keyboardShortcutManager function so it can be imported and used in other JavaScript files.
steps.hint: Use the export keyword before the function declaration to make it available for import elsewhere.
steps.expectedOutcome: The keyboardShortcutManager function is properly exported, making it available for import in other modules.
successCriteria: The keyboardShortcutManager function is exported using the export keyword.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported the keyboard shortcut manager. Now it can be imported and used in other parts of your application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct export syntax. The function needs to be exported so other files can import it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The keyboard shortcut manager isn't properly exported. Remember to use the export keyword to make the function available for import in other modules.
